stem:
The diagram shows equilateral triangle $ABC$ with $AB=BC=CA$ and midpoint $D$ of side $BC$. Omar has already shown $\triangle ABD \cong \triangle ACD$.

Which claim correctly uses that congruence?

options.text: Corresponding parts are equal, so $\angle BAD=\angle CAD$, and each angle of equilateral $\triangle ABC$ measures $60^\circ$.
Equal angles at $A$ force the congruence of $\triangle ABD$ and $\triangle ACD$, so the congruence is not needed.
Congruence of the triangles is enough even if the vertex matching is ignored.
Only sides can be equal from congruence; the $60^\circ$ angle facts need a separate rule outside corresponding parts.

teacher.key_rationale: With ABD ≅ ACD already established, corresponding parts give equal angles at A; equilateral then yields 60° angles. Saying the equal angles create the congruence reverses the given order. Ignoring vertex matching omits the correspondence condition. Restricting congruence to sides alone over-narrows corresponding parts.
teacher.figure_note: Rewrote source right triangle into equilateral ABC with median AD to match the congruence hinge.
